correctness.rationale: Kneser KG(n,k), k>=2, n>=2k, m=binom(n−1,k−1). Equality in Erdős–Ko–Rado gives, for n>2k, exactly the n maximum independent stars. Complementary simplices D_i intersect in a nonempty simplex precisely for |T|<=n−k, giving nerve sk_{n−k−1}Δ^{n−1}, homotopy wedge^m S^{n−k−1}. The equivariant Čech double complex identifies integral top homology with the kernel of simplicial boundary on that skeleton, i.e. ∧^{n−k}U_n; over Q this is hook (k,1^{n−k}). At n=2k the Kneser graph is m disjoint complementary edges and the cut complex is a cross-polytope boundary S^{m−1}. The degree of a transposition is (-1)^{binom(2k−2,k−1)/2}; central-binomial 2-adic valuation s2(k−1) makes it −1 exactly if k−1 is a 2-power. An independent permutation-pair sign computation for k=2..10 matched this parity and the trace formula; no finite test is used to establish the all-k theorem.
